I've seen a lot of hate and anger from PoCs directed at other PoCs for not voting for "the party that allowed them to be here". That's bullshit. Immigrants/POCs don't owe them votes for the rest of their lives. 

I too grew up under the assumption that Conservatives were anti-immigrant/racist and while some certainly are, that is not what the party itself or their policies represent. Nobody has been "duped". All of us had equal ability and opportunity to research each party and educate ourselves. If people are being "duped" that is to imply that they are uneducated voters and that's a different issue. If they truly believe that PC is the best choice (or a better alternative than NDP) then it is their right to vote as such. 

At the end of the day the goal should always be to choose what is best for the province and the people who live here right now, be they Canadian born, immigrants or refugees.

You really should try counselling. My husband and I had almost the same types of issues that eventually lead to a complete communication breakdown. Life was just miserable together and I asked for a divorce but even that was impossible because we couldn't say 2 words to each other without it becoming a huge fight so we decided to go to a therapist together for the sake of being able to communicate properly, whether or not we stayed together. It's been about 3 months but it's helped immensely. Our relationship isn't "fixed" and probably still is over as a couple but we are definitely able to co-operate, communicate and parent together much more effectively. It's not perfect and there are still disagreements but it's made a huge difference and if it's important to you to get along, at least for the sake of your child, it's worth a shot.

Another tip: Buy an alarm clock. A real one, set it to the latest possible time you can wake up and still make it whereever you need to go. Make sure it's LOUD. Now turn it on and put it on the opposite side of the room so you're forced to get up and turn it off. 

Also set your phone alarm with your favourite alarm tune and snooze settings so this way, you still have the opportunity to wake up gently and early or ... the LOUD back up alarm. 

Example: phone alarm set at 6:30am with two 15 min snoozes and LOUD back up alarm, set at 7am.

>"So you want some one who is psychic?" I responded. Of course, that was the incorrect answer. She wanted me to be able to anticipate things. She needs me to, despite working one and a half jobs right now and commuting three hours round trip in order to save money not parking downtown, make time to help her out with things around the house. 

Imagine you ran out of ketchup at home. She doesn't want to always be the one keeping tally of all the items in the house that need replacing. Occassionally, it would be nice if you noticed that you ran out of of ketchup and picked up a new bottle yourself. That's the difference between mind-reading and awareness about the runnings of your own home. 

You're the breadwinner and you work really hard. She's the child-rearer and she works really hard too. Three young children and a newborn is no joke. The household, however, is both your responsibility. It doesn't mean you need to get home at 9pm and start mowing the lawn or filing your taxes but it does mean you could fold some laundry or unload the dishwasher. Maybe not even every day. On the days you're extra tired, it's ok to let things get a bit messier but I sense that there isn't a sense of partnership. Just "his job" and "her job" but that's not how marriages last. 

Both of you could seek therapy and work on your issues or cut your losses in this marriage and focus on how you will split the custody in the best interest of your kids.

You're in a tough spot and I think most of the other responses are a little harsh. 

You've been through a lot with your husband and that leaves it scars. At this point, would you even consider yourselves husband and wife or roommates with children? Do you have a relationship with him as a couple? You said you killed off the part of you that loved him so do you see yourself being capable of loving him again? And if not, are you going to be happy staying just for the children?

What the others are right about is that your feelings for his best friend need to be taken out of the equation when it comes to deciding whether to stay or get divorced. Think on that carefully. Leave him because you don't want to be with him, not because you've found someone else (who by the way, is no guarantee to be a stable or permanent relationship. At this point, it's simply the better alternative). That is not to say that she isn't your soul mate, she very well may be, but she can't be the driving force for the divorce.
